narrative.overview:
The site reads like a file a careful firm would hand across a desk: a few chapters, each with one argument, set in Bodoni on forest and cream, with the evidence laid out in ruled rows rather than cards. It refuses the hero photograph, the search portal and the card grid. Proof is given by property, figures carry their basis, and every page ends in an invitation the visitor chooses to accept.

Density is low and deliberate. A strict twelve-column grid places everything, though it is never drawn: type starts on the column lines, rows split on them, and space is generous rather than decorative. Temperature, forest against cream, is the strongest move in the vocabulary and is rationed: Home makes exactly two cuts, inner pages hold one ground.

Motion is quiet and two-speed. Interface feedback is quick (180 to 300ms); narrative motion is slow (900ms to 1.6s); nothing sits between. Content is in the server HTML and readable with JavaScript off, and nothing waits on an animation.
keyCharacteristics: Forest and cream grounds, brass only for labels, figures and the italic line.
A 12-column layout grid that is felt, not drawn; full-width rows on 1px rules; no cards, shadows or fills.
Bodoni Moda 500 display with manual optical size; Libre Franklin 400 text; tracked uppercase labels.
Two motion clocks; temperature cuts that read as cuts, never fades.
Own listings only; flat placeholder frames until real photography exists.

rules.name: The Two Clocks Rule
rules.body: Interface motion is 180 to 300ms; narrative motion is 900ms to 1.6s; no duration falls between 300 and 900ms.

rules.name: The Cut Rule
rules.body: A change of ground is a hard edge, never a fade: the Home wipes, the nav on Home, and the nav on a route change all cut.

rules.name: The First Paint Rule
rules.body: No preloader, no splash, no WebGL or canvas, and the LCP element (the hero heading or hero image) never animates in.

rules.name: The Brass Ink Rule
rules.body: Brass is under 5% of any viewport: labels, figures, the italic line and the hairline. Never a fill, never a background.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: Inner pages hold one ground from the nav to the footer. Home alone makes two temperature cuts.

rules.name: The Single Weight Rule
rules.body: Display is always 500; hierarchy comes from size and leading, never from weight. Running text is always 400.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: At most one italic brass line per page (Home: one in the hero, one in the ownership chapter). Never on a section title.

rules.name: The Balanced Head Rule
rules.body: Headings balance their lines, so none ends on a single orphaned word where the column allows it.

rules.name: The Invisible Grid Rule
rules.body: The 12-column grid places everything and is never drawn; the only lines on a page are content rules and control edges.

rules.name: The Rows Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Collections of things are full-width rows on rules, never a grid of cards.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow; a surface is separated by ground or by a rule.

dos: keep brass to labels, figures, the italic line and the hairline, under 5% of a viewport.
set every position on the 12-column grid without drawing it, and keep content rules at forest/14 on cream and paper/12 on forest.
set running text at 48ch and labels at 60ch, so no line passes 75 characters.
keep text at 14px or larger at 390, `.meta` labels (10.5px) excepted.
keep figures in Bodoni 500 with lining tabular numerals, and give every figure its basis.
use flat frames until real photography exists, and serve photography through `next/image` with `priority` on the LCP image.
donts: add a preloader, splash, WebGL, canvas, count-up, marquee or scroll-driven hero scale.
animate layout properties, blur any image 600px or wider, or put any duration between 300 and 900ms.
use cards, shadows, gradients, pills, fills or glassmorphism.
put the registered name in the header, or the full seal under 120px.
show an MLS search, a map, or anything about an off-market listing beyond its area, type and tier.
set display type lighter than 500 or running text heavier than 400.
